claim: H1 multiple modalities improve flood prediction on held-out events

target.mask: Use only valid accepted in-CMA Tier A event_flood features; exclude baseline_water from positive flood target and mask permanent water/sea. Do not infer dry from absent label features.

modalities.name: terrain_only
modalities.candidate_inputs: Phase 9B v2 static terrain/hydrology feature table

modalities.name: sar_only
modalities.reason: SAR-derived candidate labels are Tier D; the 24 Nov scene may be the source scene used to prepare the UNOSAT label, making same-scene evaluation potentially circular.

modalities.name: combined
modalities.candidate_inputs: weather + terrain/hydrology + land cover; SAR only if independent and eligible

split_plan.required_for_h1: Grouped whole independent flood event/date-year holdout, then 3 km spatial blocks (100 x 100 cells) with a one-block spatial buffer between training and validation blocks; no random pixel split. The one-block buffer is a provisional conservative design choice to verify before any future scored run.
split_plan.decision: No train/test split or model fit was run. Holding out 12 or 24 Nov is at most within-episode date transfer, not independent held-out-event validation.

planned: PR-AUC where probabilistic predictions are valid
metrics.reason: H1 scoring is not supported without an independent accepted held-out flood event and consistent date/coverage alignment.

limitations: The 2021 NRSC and 2023 NDEM flood maps are not accepted digitized label rasters.
The December 2015 peak has no accepted official vector layer.
OpenCity points have unclear dates and approximate locations; they are not event-specific raster targets.
SAR-derived candidate layers remain Tier D and are excluded from scoring.
This feasibility record is not a model evaluation or evidence that modalities improve skill.
